# Preface {.unnumbered}

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(webexercises)
```

This book is an introduction to the analysis of social and behavioral data using R. It is designed for complete beginners. No prior programming experience is assumed.

The book is organized into sections, each containing several chapters. You can read the chapters in order, or jump to a specific topic using the table of contents on the left.

## How to use this book {.unnumbered}

Each chapter contains:

- explanations of concepts, written for readers with no programming background;
- examples of R code that you can copy and run on your own machine;
- a short set of multiple-choice questions at the end. Click an option to receive immediate feedback.

## What you will need {.unnumbered}

To follow along you will need:

- a computer running Windows, macOS, or Linux;
- R (the language and computing engine);
- RStudio (a working environment for R, optional but strongly recommended);
- an internet connection to install additional R packages.

The first chapters will guide you through the installation of these tools.

## Section 1: Getting Started Properly {.unnumbered}

Section 1 lays out the foundations: what R is, how to install it, what the different file types are, and how to perform basic operations. By the end of Section 1 you will have a solid mental model of the R ecosystem and you will be ready to start working with real data.

Additional sections will be added as the book grows.
